reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in combining structured public datasets—shot locations, play-by-play logs, matchup tracking, and biometric data—into a single per-shot representation. This fusion enables training a neural network (ShotNet) to estimate shot value as a function of spatial and contextual features. The resulting shot value estimates are then used within a game-tree framework where each possession is modeled as a sequence of decisions. An expectimax search algorithm evaluates potential shot paths, guided by the learned shot values and constrained by computational efficiency via branch-and-bound pruning. This architecture allows real-time decision support for offensive plays while maintaining alignment with observed professional performance metrics. Failure modes include misalignment between public data and real-world dynamics, or overfitting to specific data regimes not representative of broader tactical diversity.
